name: Tamar
bio:
Tamar is Judah's daughter-in-law, married in turn to his firstborn son Er and then his second son Onan, both of whom the LORD put to death for wickedness, leaving her widowed twice (Genesis 38:6-10). By the custom of the time, Judah should have given his third son Shelah to her as a husband to raise up offspring for his dead brothers, but fearing Shelah might meet the same fate, he kept delaying, leaving Tamar waiting as a widow in her father's house indefinitely (Genesis 38:11, 14).

Seeing that Judah had failed to keep his word, Tamar disguised herself as a prostitute and sat waiting along a road she knew Judah would travel. Not recognizing her, Judah slept with her, leaving behind his seal, cord, and staff as a pledge for payment. Three months later, when Judah heard his daughter-in-law was pregnant, he ordered her burned to death — until Tamar produced the pledge items, proving the father was Judah himself. Judah then admitted, "She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son" (Genesis 38:24-26). Tamar later gave birth to twins, Perez and Zerah; Perez's line continued down to King David and is recorded in the genealogy of Jesus Christ (Ruth 4:18-22; Matthew 1:3). Though Tamar's story is morally complex and difficult, it also shows how God's providence carried forward the Messianic bloodline through a woman who had been wronged and marginalized.
